response:
The ICC (Intraclass Correlation Coefficient) measures how similar observations within the same cluster are to one another — equivalently, it is the proportion of total variance that is attributable to between-cluster (level-2) differences.

The formula is: ICC = σ²_u / (σ²_u + σ²_e), where σ²_u is the between-cluster (level-2) variance and σ²_e is the within-cluster (level-1, residual) variance. An ICC of 0.10 means 10% of the total variance lies between clusters.

The ICC also determines the design effect and is a key input to power analysis for clustered designs. You obtain σ²_u and σ²_e from the variance components table (the 'Random effects' section in lme4 or statsmodels output) and plug them into the formula above.
